d.title: Six kinds of group key, and only the first is a column
d.caption: **Everything after the first row is a key you did not have to add a column for** — which is the practical value of the section, because the usual instinct is to create a `month` column, group by it, then drop it. The callable form is the general one: any function of the index label can be a key, so “weekday against weekend” is a lambda rather than a column. **`pd.Grouper` is the groupby spelling of resample**, and it is what lets a time bucket be one key among several — month *and* product — which plain `resample` cannot express.

d.title: An instant, a duration, a span - and the parse that guesses
d.caption: **Most time-series confusion is a Timestamp standing in for a Period: an instant being used to mean a whole day or month.** Monthly data indexed by the first of the month is a point pretending to be a span, and a PeriodIndex says what is meant. **The parsing row is the one that corrupts data silently.** Without `format=`, pandas infers the layout from the first value and applies it to the rest — so a column where 01/03 comes before 13/03 may be read month-first, and then 13/03 either raises or becomes NaT. State the format.
